messages:
alex: quick sync — propose a small "handshake protocol" for swapping from FlashAttn v2 -> v3. goal: zero-surprise perf, preserve kv-prefix semantics, and avoid batching-induced tail spikes. I put a short plan here: https://rwd.internal/notes/flash-handshake :thumbsup:

maria: skimmed the doc. grabbed microbench numbers for opt-2.7b on A100 (seq=512/1024): v2 med=10.8ms p95=18.6ms, v3 med=9.9ms p95=20.1ms. so v3 improves median but p95 regressed at higher seqs with large batches. details: 
```
./bench --model opt-2.7b --seq 1024 --batch 8 --kernels flashv2,flashv3
# results: v2  med 12.4ms p95 19.3ms; v3 med 11.1ms p95 21.0ms
```

ryan: noted. looks like v3 has slightly different kv/cache interaction causing higher tail when many prefix-hits combine with large batch sizes. on paged-attn those merges are more expensive.

jin: suggestion: add a short-lived kernel handshake where runtime checks three signals before choosing v3: (1) seq <= 512 OR (2) batch_size <= 4 OR (3) kv_prefix_hit_rate > 0.95. otherwise stay on v2. we can implement as a selector with feature flags. sample ff: `ff_flashattn_selector=handshake_v1`.

perf-bot: smoke run @3475432140: smoke-suite(opt-2.7b, 1k reqs) -> overall: pass; p50 -4.2% (good), p95 +3.1% (regression), mem +1.0%, kv_hitrate 0.973. attaching brief perf log.

nina: batching heuristics are important here. if runtime keeps `max_batch_time_ms=8` for v2, might need to lower to `5` for v3 when selector picks it to avoid long assemble waits. otherwise p95 climbs. also consider lowering `max_batch_tokens` for sequences >512.

ryan: ops concern — paged-attn + v3 changes KV cache lifecycle slightly. we must ensure cached KV IDs survive kernel swap. proposal: when selector flips kernel mid-request, force a small in-memory handshake that validates cached offsets; if mismatch, fallback to v2 and emit metric `kernelswap.kv_mismatch`.

alex: ops-bot can we get a rollout play stub? want to ramp v3 to 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50 with automated rollback on p95 +7% or kv_miss > 0.5%

ops-bot: acknowledged. creating canary pipeline: `canary/demo-flashattn-v3` with steps: traffic 1% (30m), verify latency & errors, 5% (1h), 20% (2h), 50% (4h). auto-rollback triggers: p95 increase >=7% OR error rate >=0.5% OR kv_mismatch count >= 5 in 10m.

maria: actionable perf tweaks to try during canary: 1) v3: reduce `max_batch_time_ms` to 5ms for seq>512, 2) enable `prefetch_kv_pages=true` for paged-attn, 3) disable continuous batching for routes with high kv_hit_rate. quick bench shows p95 improves by ~6% with these.

jin: config flags we should add to feature matrix: `flashattn.selector=handshake_v1`, `flashattn.v3.batch_time_ms_override`, `flashattn.v3.prefetch_kv`, `flashattn.kv.swap_fallback=true`.

alex: summary / next steps: 
- [ ] jin implement selector + metric `kernelswap.kv_mismatch` (assign jin)
- [ ] ops-bot create canary pipeline (assigned to ops-bot)
- [ ] maria run staged perf with batching overrides and post results (assigned maria)
- [ ] nina update batching config defaults for v3 (assigned nina)
- [ ] ryan validate kv prefix stability tests in integration harness (assigned ryan)

If everyone OK we'll aim to flip selector to handshake_v1 in canary tomorrow 09:00 PT.
